evidence.text: The 肉 entry displays material in oracle-bone, Chu bamboo-and-silk, and Small Seal categories and states that the ancient graph was shaped like a piece of meat. It gives no individual specimen dates or detailed graphic sequence.

evidence.text: The received Shuowen text defines 肉 as 胾肉 and calls it pictographic. The later Duan Yucai annotation interprets 胾 as a large piece of animal meat and says the graph was extended to bodily-character compounds and senses involving the solid part of a ring and musical usage. These are historical dictionary interpretations, not independently dated evidence for the proposed semantic links.
evidence.kind: historical dictionary text and later annotation
evidence.title: 肉 ròu - 漢典

evidence.field: 康熙字典／書證／字源字形
evidence.text: The entry cites transmitted examples for meat and flesh, fruit pulp, ring-body, and musical senses, and lists specimen identifiers under oracle-bone, Chu manuscript, Shuowen seal, Qin slip, and clerical-script headings. The entry does not establish the exact date of each cited wording or that its displayed headings form a fully documented sequence.
evidence.title: 肉 ròu - 漢典

evidence.field: 異體字研訂／形體資料表
evidence.text: The entry cites the Shuowen pictographic account and discusses graphic variants including 宍 and 𠕎. It says 𠕎 is considered to derive through clerical transformation from the Shuowen seal form. This supports that variant-specific relationship, not an entire ancient-to-modern graphic sequence.

search_audit.outcome: Inspected the Academia Sinica paleographic entry, Taiwan Ministry of Education variant entry, and Han Dian character entry. They support the meat-pictograph analysis and list script categories or variants, but do not provide a fully dated graphic sequence.

search_audit.query: 肉 oracle bone script pictograph meat Shuowen graph development
search_audit.outcome: Inspected Shuowen.org and Han Dian; Shuowen.org page returned no readable text in this session, while Han Dian exposed the received Shuowen wording, annotation, script categories, cited senses and phonological notes.

Opened the exact 肉-seal.svg file page. It identifies the drawing as Shuowen seal-style, names historical source leads and a Hanziyuan model image, documents 2007 uploads and gives public-domain terms.
Search/category results surfaced the file, but opening the exact Radical 135 page returned an internal error. The file's contents and rights were therefore not independently verified.

gaps: No inspected source dates individual oracle-bone or manuscript specimens or gives a complete, critically supported sequence of graphic changes. The available category labels should not be treated as a specimen chronology.

The dictionaries cite uses for meat, bodily flesh, fruit pulp, ring-body, and musical senses, but exact composition dates and earliest attestations for each sense remain unestablished; no chronology or semantic path is inferred from gloss order.
The dossier's competing proposed deeper word-etymologies remain unresolved. The graph's pictographic origin does not settle the spoken word's deeper history.
The exact Commons Radical 135 page failed to open; its image identity, attribution, and rights remain unverified. The 肉-seal.svg page is a verified alternative redraw, not an ancient artifact image.
The official Unicode Unihan U+8089 record was attempted but inaccessible. Supplied local Unihan and Baxter–Sagart rows remain local data and were not externally verified in this research session.
